components.name: Primary Estimate Button
components.description: The red action for estimate starts and form submission.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { min-height: 50px; padding: .8rem 1.25rem; border: 0; border-radius: 0; background: var(--red); color: #fff; font: 800 .78rem/1.1 var(--body); cursor: pointer; transition: transform .22s var(--ease-out), box-shadow .22s var(--ease-out), background .22s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #c92424; transform: translateY(-2px); box-shadow: 0 10px 24px rgba(3,5,15,.24); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--red); outline-offset: 4px; }

components.name: Secondary Service Button
components.description: The royal-blue action inside a selected service path.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { min-height: 50px; padding: .8rem 1.25rem; border: 0; border-radius: 0; background: var(--blue); color: #fff; font: 800 .78rem/1.1 var(--body); cursor: pointer; transition: transform .22s var(--ease-out), box-shadow .22s var(--ease-out); } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); box-shadow: 0 10px 24px rgba(3,5,15,.24); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--red); outline-offset: 4px; }

components.name: Selected Service Path
components.description: The large ruled choice that separates landscape and concrete intent.
components.css: .ds-service-choice { min-height: 160px; width: 100%; padding: 2rem; border: 0; border-radius: 0; background: var(--blue); color: var(--cream); text-align: left; cursor: pointer; } .ds-service-choice strong { display: block; font: 400 clamp(2.2rem,4vw,4.2rem)/1 var(--display); } .ds-service-choice span { display: block; max-width: 40ch; margin-top: .8rem; font: 400 .88rem/1.55 var(--body); } .ds-service-choice:hover { background: #2525cb; } .ds-service-choice:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--red); outline-offset: 4px; }

components.name: Estimate Field
components.description: A square, high-clarity field for project details.
components.html: <label class="ds-field-label">PROJECT LOCATION<input class="ds-field" placeholder="City or neighborhood"></label>
components.css: .ds-field-label { display: block; color: var(--ink); font: 800 .78rem/1.1 var(--body); letter-spacing: .05em; } .ds-field { display: block; width: 100%; margin-top: .45rem; padding: .86rem .9rem; border: 1px solid #a9a794; border-radius: 0; background: #fff; color: var(--ink); font: 400 1rem/1.55 var(--body); } .ds-field:hover { border-color: var(--ink); } .ds-field:focus-visible { border-color: var(--blue); outline: 3px solid rgba(1,0,128,.16); }

components.name: Project Proof Card
components.description: A dark proof field with a ruled caption; the live page supplies verified project imagery.
components.css: .ds-proof-card { margin: 0; overflow: hidden; border-radius: 0; background: var(--night); color: #fff; } .ds-proof-image { min-height: 180px; background: linear-gradient(135deg,var(--blue),var(--night)); } .ds-proof-card figcaption { padding: 1.1rem; background: rgba(5,8,21,.9); font: 400 .82rem/1.4 var(--body); } .ds-proof-card strong { display: block; color: var(--cream); font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: .07em; } .ds-proof-card:focus-within { outline: 3px solid var(--red); outline-offset: 4px; }

components.name: Mobile Contact Bar
components.description: Two equal actions that keep phone and estimate paths reachable on mobile.
components.html: CALLREQUEST ESTIMATE
components.css: .ds-mobile-actions { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; min-height: 66px; background: var(--cream); box-shadow: 0 -8px 28px rgba(0,0,0,.2); } .ds-mobile-actions a { display: grid; place-items: center; padding: .8rem; color: var(--night); font: 800 .82rem/1.1 var(--body); text-decoration: none; } .ds-mobile-actions a:last-child { background: var(--red); color: #fff; } .ds-mobile-actions a:hover { text-decoration: underline; } .ds-mobile-actions a:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--red); outline-offset: -4px; }

narrative.overview:
This system follows the ground itself: midnight terrain, cream plan paper, royal-blue contour fields, and one red survey mark. It feels capable and site-aware rather than decorative, using open bands, ruled choices, and clipped photographic windows to connect landscape and concrete as one coordinated exterior scope.

Scale and contrast do the heavy work. Condensed display type makes decisive terrain-scale statements, while Public Sans carries practical detail. Verified project photography remains visible and materially grounded; contour lines, survey points, and process runways provide the recurring connective gesture.
keyCharacteristics: Monumental condensed display type against dark terrain fields.
Cream plan-paper surfaces separated by precise blue or ink rules.
Royal blue carries structure; red marks decisions and action.
Clipped real-work imagery crossed by contour and grade-line geometry.
Square controls, open section bands, and explicit mobile action paths.

rules.name: The Survey Mark Rule
rules.body: Red identifies action or a single point of emphasis; it does not become a broad decorative wash outside the estimate stage.

rules.name: The Terrain Scale Rule
rules.body: Anton is reserved for decisive spatial hierarchy; paragraphs and interface detail stay in Public Sans.

rules.name: The Follow-the-Grade Rule
rules.body: Every layout shift must preserve the visual path from site condition to service choice, real work, process, and estimate action.

rules.name: The Flat Plan Rule
rules.body: Rules and color changes establish most hierarchy; shadows appear only where an object must visibly sit above its field.

dos: Do use verified project imagery as primary proof and keep crops large enough to read the relationship between grade, structure, and finish.
Do preserve strong cream-on-night contrast, square controls, and red as the focused action marker.
Do translate the horizontal grade-line journey into a vertical, equally legible sequence on mobile.
Do keep reduced-motion users in the complete final visual state.
donts: Don't replace the open bands and ruled service choice with a generic rounded-card grid.
Don't spread red across multiple competing decorative elements in the same field.
Don't round buttons, inputs, or proof containers into soft product-UI shapes.
Don't use stock imagery or decorative landscape photos in place of verified Omega project work.
